# FAIR-bioHeaders Tools (Java)

> Java library for reading, checksum-verifying and JSON-Schema-validating FAIR-bioHeaders provenance headers embedded in bioinformatics files: FHR for reference genome FASTA and GFA, FHP for protein FASTA, and FHGFF3 for GFF3 annotations. A header is a block of YAML lines at the top of the file (`;~` in FASTA, `#~` in GFA and GFF3), validated against a draft/2020-12 JSON Schema and covered by a SHA-512/256 checksum of the file's exact bytes. This repository is the Java member of the per-language library family; the normative definitions are in FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification and the reference implementation with header writing is the Python `fair-bioheaders` toolkit.

Key facts (this library bundles contract copies of FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification v0.6.0 as its current release; selection follows the shared rules V1-V6):

- Schema versions: FHR `schemaVersion: '2.1'`, FHP `'1.2'`, FHGFF3 `'1.2'`; cite the versioned w3id URLs `https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/{fhr,fhp,fhgff3}/v0.6.0`. A file's `schema` value selects the schema it is validated against; an unknown release is reported as unsupported-version, never re-checked against another schema.
- **Never write or edit a checksum by hand.** This library only verifies (read + validate + checksum-verify); header creation belongs to `bioheaders combine` in the Python toolkit. Changing any byte except the checksum line invalidates it.
- The checksum is SHA-512/256 (the JDK `MessageDigest` algorithm, not truncated SHA-512) over the file's exact bytes minus the one root-level `checksum` line and its terminator, padded standard base64, compared as exact strings (FORMAT.md R1-R5). Gzip/bgzip files are verified through their decompressed bytes.
- In FASTA, header values containing `>` or `@` should be written as YAML escapes `\x3E` and `\x40` (rule R11), because kseq-based readers start a record at those characters; a file with raw characters stays valid and this reader warns. YAML readers return the real characters.
- Many FASTA tools reject a leading `;~` block, including samtools faidx (htslib), pysam `FastaFile`, bedtools getfasta, Picard, Bowtie2, HISAT2, STAR, salmon and Biopython's default `fasta` format. Use `bioheaders strip` (Python toolkit) to make a plain copy, or `SeqIO.parse(path, "fasta-pearson")` in Biopython. GFF3 and GFA tools surveyed accept `#~` lines.
- Plain YAML scalars must read identically under YAML 1.1 and YAML 1.2 (rule R12): `010`, `1_000`, `1:30`, `yes`, `1e3` and explicit tags are invalid; the reader enforces this with its own resolver pinned to the reference toolkit's behavior, not the parser's.
- Extension fields (rule R15, from FHR 2.1 and FHP/FHGFF3 1.1): top-level `^x-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$` keys are accepted and carry no standard meaning; every other unknown key is invalid and nested objects stay closed.
- This build retains historical FHT/FHGM draft pins (rule V7); family FHT 1.0 and native FHGM 0.1 publication do not promote these consumer pins. For these pinned draft forms: no **released/registered** `schemaVersion` (the FHT draft contract itself requires a `schemaVersion: "1.0"` field in the header — what is absent is a `schemaVersion` registered in the shared `schemas/versions.json`), no w3id URL, no registry row. Header types are registry data (`schemas/bundled.json` `types`). **FHT is registered as a pinned draft** (FHT-Specification commit 86438f21c3a17a58334c97aed4955be1a2393522, SHA-256 4156353aa6d077fee2d2c69be4e17859b8e4f81bb10824f3c87f6701de196e7a): readable only through explicit opt-in (`Options.builder().enableDraftContracts(true)`, `verify --experimental-drafts`, `--draft FHT`, system property `org.fairbioheaders.experimental.drafts`, environment variable `FAIR_BIOHEADERS_EXPERIMENTAL_DRAFTS`), re-digest-checked at bundle build, and warned on per record with the commit and digest named. Gate closed = rule V5 (read as FHR, near-miss warning), byte-identical to the released-only reader. Reading a draft is not adoption, support or release, and its 82 vectors are counted in a separate labelled job, never in the 291. **FHGM is registered as an `embedded-records` draft**: it is not a header type - its records ride inside an FHGFF3 header under `x-fhgm-models`, the file stays routed by its released FHGFF3 citation, and `FhgmModels` (opt-in, two further pinned contract files, each with its own commit: record contract `b7075e58…` at commit `06176262…`, transport overlay `533b3120…` (3 191 B, the dual-base overlay with URL-keyed selection and the widened model layer of FHGM#29) at commit `019bc29e…`, both of FHGM-Specification) applies the draft's model-level rules K1-K6, refusing any carrier whose base schema or checksum fails first (B1). Its 62 vectors and 10 rule tests run in the labelled draft job (this library scores K4 natively while FHGM#22/#27/#28, FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification#241 and JS#11 leave the K4 abstention question open upstream: a pass under these bytes carries FHGM#29's widened model-layer meaning, and 4 FHT vectors remain candidate-unreviewed); the suite's separate FHGFF3-1.2 `base_matrix.json` lane is not run here. See docs/CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md.

## Using it

```java
import org.fairbioheaders.BioHeaders;
import org.fairbioheaders.VerifyResult;

VerifyResult r = new BioHeaders().verifyFile(Path.of("genome.fhr.fasta"));
r.isValid(); r.status();          // VALID | INVALID | UNSUPPORTED_VERSION
r.computedChecksum();             // recomputed SHA-512/256 (R3/R4)
r.metadata();                     // parsed header as a Jackson JsonNode
r.issues();                       // rule-labelled errors and warnings (R11, R14, V5, V6, V7)
r.parentLinkVerdicts();           // CHECKED_PASS | CHECKED_FAIL | UNCHECKED, per derivedFrom entry
```

CLI: `./mvnw -DskipTests package`, then `java -jar target/fair-bioheaders-java-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar verify FILE...` (runtime dependencies are copied to `target/lib/`, which the jar's manifest references; exit 0 only when every file verifies).

## Scope boundaries

- Implemented: containers FASTA/GFA/GFF3, FORMAT.md R1-R8 and R10-R14, FHGFF3.md G1-G3 placement and contract checks, SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md V1-V6 selection plus the opt-in V7 draft lane (FHT and FHGM, pinned), draft/2020-12 validation with format assertions, per-entry `derivedFrom` parent-link verdicts (`ParentLinks`, `verify --parent`), bundled frozen schema copies v0.3.0-v0.6.0 and three pinned draft contract files, all with SHA-256 provenance.
- Not implemented: header writing, conversion, stripping, faidx, HTML microdata and JSON-LD bindings, and GFF3 feature-line validation (use gff3-validator). FHGM records are read only through the pinned opt-in draft lane - never as support. `docs/STATUS.md` records the shared-conformance results (228 embedded-header vectors run; the 63 microdata/JSON-LD vectors are declared not run) and the separate draft-lane results (82 FHT vectors, 62 FHGM vectors, plus FHGM's 1.2 matrix lane declared not run); `docs/CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md` is the type × operation × serialization × version statement with every hole named.
- Acceptance is the shared conformance suite (291 vectors at the v0.6.0 tag CI pins; the ledger reads newer manifests' own counts) of FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification (`conformance/manifest.json`); run with `./mvnw test -Dfh.spec.dir=<spec-checkout>`. Default behavior is additionally pinned by a committed fingerprint of the released-contract reading (`src/test/resources/golden/default-behavior-v0.6.0.json`, `DefaultBehaviorGoldenTest`).

## Independent review and human-only merges (maintainer direction, 2026-11-20)

The [Round 16 policy](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/issues/211#issuecomment-7042896529)
supersedes the former conditional agent-merge authorization of 2026-11-16/18 and
the #268 authority links recorded under it. **Agents must never merge pull
requests in this repository; a human performs every merge.** Do not enable
auto-merge, enter a merge queue, use another agent or service as a merge proxy,
or push directly to the default branch as a substitute for merging a PR. Model
review never grants an agent merge authority; preserve platform protections and
do not forge approval or work around repository permissions.

Every PR receives independent review from another actual model. A different
model family is preferred (for example Codex or Gemini reviewing Qwen work, or
Qwen reviewing Codex work), but family diversity is a preference, not a hard
requirement; a second session of the same model is not another model. Record
actual author/reviewer model identities and never invent review provenance.

Agents keep monitoring CI and fixing failures and actionable review findings:
read the overall review and every inline finding, fix in new commits, reply with
disposition and evidence, resolve handled threads and acknowledge clean reviews.
Validate the current head after changes and hand the human exact head/base,
review, CI, dependency and remaining-risk information. Missing, failed and
NOT_RUN checks are not passes. This grants no contract adoption, curator
acceptance, release, publication or deployment authority — those gates are
unchanged. Earlier rounds' authorized merges and dated receipts remain accurate
historical facts, not future permission.
